$doc: Vyomi capability registry — RDS. See s3.json for the contract.

rds.instance.deletion-protection.title: Deletion protection
limitations: ModifyDBInstance applies a fixed subset of fields (class, storage, engine version, backup retention, master password); other settings are stored and returned but not individually validated.

rds.data-api.title: SQL execution (Query editor / RDS Data API)
limitations: The data plane is a real engine (sqlite3 by default, PGlite real Postgres on Nano) reached only through the RDS Data API (ExecuteStatement/BatchExecuteStatement) — Vyomi does not expose the Postgres/MySQL wire protocol directly, so an unmodified psycopg2/mysqlclient TCP connection cannot reach it.

BeginTransaction/ExecuteStatement(transactionId)/CommitTransaction/RollbackTransaction are REAL cross-call transactions — a statement that carries the transaction id runs against a connection held open since BeginTransaction and is not committed until CommitTransaction (discarded on Rollback); how many can be open at once is capped by the instance's own max_connections. A statement reading a different connection while a transaction is uncommitted can see a 'database is locked' error on the sqlite engine (Nano's default) instead of Postgres-style MVCC snapshot isolation — a sqlite-specific gap, not present on the PGlite (real Postgres) engine.

rds.subnet-groups.title: DB subnet groups
limitations: Subnet IDs and the VPC are stored and returned exactly as given; Vyomi does not validate that they exist in a real VPC (it does not model EC2/VPC in depth for RDS).

rds.parameter-groups.title: DB parameter groups and parameters
limitations: Parameters are stored and returned exactly as modified (ModifyDBParameterGroup round-trips through DescribeDBParameters). max_connections is ENFORCED against the RDS Data API's real transactions (rds.data-api) — BeginTransaction on an instance already at its parameter group's max_connections is rejected, not silently accepted; lowering/raising the value genuinely changes that ceiling. Every other parameter (shared_buffers, log_min_duration_statement, innodb_buffer_pool_size, …) remains stored/returned only, with no effect on the underlying SQL engine.

rds.events.title: Events (DescribeEvents)
limitations: Vyomi logs its own control-plane actions (create/modify/delete/lifecycle/snapshot); it does not generate the full category list AWS produces (e.g. failover, low-storage).

rds.proxy.title: RDS Proxy
limitations: Creating, listing and deleting a DB proxy record is real and stateful; Vyomi does not actually proxy connections through it — apps still connect straight to the instance's own endpoint.

rds.option-groups.title: Option groups
limitations: Option group metadata CRUD is real; adding/removing individual options within a group is not modeled — Vyomi has no engine-specific option catalogue (e.g. Oracle APEX, SQL Server TDE).

rds.event-subscriptions.title: Event subscriptions
limitations: An enabled subscription whose SourceType/EventCategories match really publishes to its SnsTopicArn (through the same sns_core.publish_arn seam EventBridge targets use) when the matching RDS control-plane event fires — not just a stored record. Delivery covers the same control-plane events rds.events logs (create/modify/delete/lifecycle/snapshot); AWS's fuller category list (e.g. failover, low-storage) isn't generated, matching rds.events' own scope.

rds.automated-backups.title: Automated backups
limitations: The current-region automated backup window is derived from the live instance's retention setting (DescribeDBInstanceAutomatedBackups); cross-region replication of backups and backups retained after instance deletion are not modeled.

rds.monitoring.title: CloudWatch metrics on the DB instance detail page
limitations: DatabaseConnections (the instance's real count of currently open RDS Data API transactions) and ReadIOPS/WriteIOPS (a real count of SELECT vs. write statements actually executed through the RDS Data API / query editor) are genuine datapoints pushed to CloudWatch (AWS/RDS namespace) as the activity happens — GetMetricStatistics/GetMetricData return real series, not synthetic ones.

CPUUtilization, FreeStorageSpace and FreeableMemory have no real analogue in Vyomi — there is no virtualized compute, disk or memory allocation behind a DB instance to measure, so the Monitoring tab shows them as unavailable rather than inventing numbers.

rds.logs.title: DB log files
limitations: Vyomi derives one real error-log file per DB instance (error/postgresql.log or error/mysql-error-running.log, via the native DescribeDBLogFiles/DownloadDBLogFilePortion actions) from genuine SQL execution failures raised through the RDS Data API / query editor — an instance with no failed statements has an empty log, not a fabricated one.

The sqlite3 / PGlite data plane has no general engine process of its own, so startup, checkpoint and slow-query logging that a real Postgres/MySQL log would contain is not generated — only statement errors are captured.

rds.replication.title: Read replicas, Multi-AZ failover, connected compute resources, security group rules
limitations: CreateDBInstanceReadReplica/PromoteReadReplica are real, stateful: a replica is a genuine, independent DB instance, linked bidirectionally to its source, that cannot be deleted while replicas exist. Every autocommit write (ExecuteStatement without a transactionId) on the source is really replayed against each replica's own engine as it happens, so a replica's data genuinely reflects the source's writes — statements run inside an explicit BeginTransaction are NOT forwarded (replicas are independent engines, not a shared WAL), so lag is effectively zero for the path that is replicated and undefined for the path that isn't.

RebootDBInstance with ForceFailover=true genuinely swaps a Multi-AZ instance's live AvailabilityZone with its secondary (rejected with InvalidParameterCombination on a non-Multi-AZ instance) — a real state change, not a stored flag.

Connected compute resources and Security group rules are read directly off the real EC2/VPC core (core/vpc_core.py) by security-group membership — genuine cross-service correlation, not fabricated rows. Vyomi does not model a literal second physical storage volume for Multi-AZ, so failover carries no data (nothing is lost, since Nano's data plane isn't volume-replicated to begin with).

rds.reserved-instances.title: Reserved instances (purchase)
limitations: PurchaseReservedDBInstancesOffering records a real, stateful reservation (DescribeReservedDBInstances lists it); Vyomi has no billing system and no reserved-instance-offering catalogue, so the console's purchase wizard (pricing, terms, offering ids) is not built — call the action directly with a reservation id.

rds.capacity-reservations.title: Capacity reservations
limitations: Capacity reservations are a capacity-market/billing construct Vyomi does not model.

rds.zero-etl.title: Zero-ETL integrations
limitations: CreateIntegration/DeleteIntegration/DescribeIntegrations is real, stateful metadata CRUD; Vyomi does not run the actual cross-service replication pipeline into Redshift, so the console's create wizard (picking a real Redshift target) is not built — call the action directly with source/target ARNs.

rds.custom-engine-versions.title: RDS Custom engine versions
limitations: CreateCustomDBEngineVersion/DeleteCustomDBEngineVersion/DescribeDBEngineVersions registers real, stateful install-media metadata; RDS Custom itself (the customer-managed EC2 instance the engine actually runs on) is out of Vyomi's scope entirely — the console's create wizard is not built.

rds.recommendations.title: RDS recommendations
limitations: DescribeDBRecommendations derives four real advisories from each instance's own live configuration (no Multi-AZ, an outdated CA certificate, automated backups disabled, deletion protection disabled); Vyomi has no general analysis engine, so it does not generate the full category of recommendations AWS's own monitoring produces (e.g. storage autoscaling, parameter tuning).

rds.exports-to-s3.title: Exports to Amazon S3
limitations: StartExportTask writes the snapshot's real table data as gzip-compressed Apache Parquet into the simulator's OWN S3 store (never AWS) in AWS's layout — <prefix>/<task>/<database>/<schema>.<table>/part-00000-<id>.gz.parquet plus export_info_<task>.json and export_tables_info_<task>_from_1_to_<N>.json. Offline the Parquet writer is pyarrow; in Nano it is the vendored parquet-wasm 0.7.1 + apache-arrow 18.1.0 (lazy-loaded on the first export). If the Parquet engine is unavailable or fails, or the bucket doesn't exist, the task FAILS with a FailureCause — there is no fallback format.

Column types are mapped approximately to five Arrow types (int64, float64, bool, string, binary): dates/timestamps, decimals/numeric, JSON and other engine types are exported as strings, and a sqlite column whose stored values don't fit its declared type is exported as a string column.

One Parquet file (one partition) per table; IamRoleArn and KmsKeyId are recorded but not enforced (the files are not KMS-encrypted). Exports complete synchronously (STARTING/IN_PROGRESS are never observed). A snapshot taken before the engine captured snapshot contents (or adopted from the pre-v4 offline handler) carries no table data — exporting it fails with that cause.

rds.certificate-rotation.title: Certificate authority rotation
limitations: CACertificateIdentifier is validated on CreateDBInstance/ModifyDBInstance against a real, small CA catalog (DescribeCertificates) — the same identifiers and validity windows AWS publishes (rds-ca-rsa2048-g1, rds-ca-rsa4096-g1, rds-ca-ecc384-g1, the retired rds-ca-2019); an unknown id is rejected (CertificateNotFound), and any instance whose CA differs from the current default is flagged on the certificate-update page with its REAL ValidFrom/ValidTill (no more placeholder dates), with a working 'Apply update now' that really calls ModifyDBInstance. Vyomi does not enforce wall-clock cert expiry at connection time — a cert past its ValidTill doesn't actually block anything.

rds.iam-roles.title: IAM role association for RDS features (AddRoleToDBInstance / RemoveRoleFromDBInstance / AssociatedRoles)
limitations: The role must exist in Vyomi's IAM and trust rds.amazonaws.com, and the feature must be one the engine supports (checked against AWS's per-engine list); associations are stored and returned like the real API. The database engines in Vyomi do not actually assume the role, so s3Import/s3Export through the role is not performed — S3 exports use Vyomi's own export-task path (rds.exports-to-s3).

rds.cloudwatch-alarms.title: CloudWatch alarms for a DB instance (create, list, delete, SNS action) in the Logs & events tab
limitations: Real CloudWatch alarms on AWS/RDS metrics with the DBInstanceIdentifier dimension. Only DatabaseConnections, ReadIOPS and WriteIOPS carry data (see rds.monitoring); alarms on CPUUtilization, FreeStorageSpace or FreeableMemory exist but stay INSUFFICIENT_DATA because Vyomi has no virtualized compute/disk to measure.

rds.service-quotas.title: Dashboard and Service quotas pages (DescribeAccountAttributes: default quotas + live usage)
limitations: Quota maxima are AWS's default RDS quotas for us-east-1 and cannot be raised (no Service Quotas increase workflow). Usage is counted from the live store (instances, allocated storage, subnet groups, snapshots, roles, proxies); the dashboard's DB clusters count is 0 because Aurora clusters aren't modeled.

rds.restore-from-s3.title: Restore from S3
limitations: RestoreDBInstanceFromS3 validates like the real API (MySQL only, required parameters, role ARN, existing identifier, missing bucket or empty prefix -> InvalidS3BucketFault) and builds a new instance from backup files in the simulator's own S3. Real RDS reads a Percona XtraBackup physical backup, which cannot be replayed here: Vyomi reads .sql / .sql.gz logical dumps (mysqldump output is normalised for the engine: LOCK/UNLOCK/SET/USE statements, ENGINE=/CHARSET=/AUTO_INCREMENT= options and inline KEY lines are dropped) and, on the offline appliance only, the Parquet files of an RDS snapshot export. Auto-increment behaviour, stored routines, triggers, views and users in a dump are not preserved by the instance's engine, a failing statement leaves the instance in incompatible-restore, and an XtraBackup file is refused.

rds.data-migrations.title: Data migrations (AWS DMS between simulator databases)
limitations: Real DMS control plane (core/dms_core.py, target AmazonDMSv20160101): replication instances, source/target endpoints, TestConnection, replication tasks with selection-rule TableMappings, DescribeTableStatistics. An endpoint's ServerName must resolve to a simulator RDS instance; StartReplicationTask really creates the selected tables on the target instance and copies the rows.

CDC is 'CDC-lite': a running cdc / full-load-and-cdc task re-reads the source and applies row-level inserts, updates and deletes (keyed on the primary key) whenever the task is described, reloaded, resumed or stopped - there is no WAL/binlog reader, so changes appear when polled rather than instantly.

Table and column discovery uses the simulator's SQL engine catalog (sqlite on the default engine). Not modelled: transformation rules, data validation, LOB settings, premigration assessments, DMS Serverless, non-SQL endpoint engines (accepted for configuration but TestConnection fails), schema conversion.
